method: For each blocked component, sketch the minimum-viable wrapper assuming the most generous interpretation of any candidate shard's role. Compare LOC vs original blocked spec.

wrappers.wrapper_loc_estimate: infinite (any 'wrapper' would have to re-implement 100% of the matmul + tanh-gelu + LCG + clamp + JSONL emit logic in Python, since no shard contributes anything; this is just rewriting Comp 1 in Python, NOT wrapping a shard)
wrappers.blocker: shards do not perform tensor projection or float emission

wrappers.wrapper_loc_estimate: ~80 LOC scaffold but the proxy signal is corr=-0.31 (noise) so the wrapper must STILL re-implement the LCG random projection + L1 gate + phi_star + L2 + mind_step in Python to actually compute correct values. That's ~140 LOC of Python, on top of which calling hxc_a25 adds zero information.
wrappers.blocker: a25 classify's rule_density_per100 carries no L1-band signal (Phase 4 measured)

wrappers.wrapper_loc_estimate: ~95 LOC of pure Python (essentially line-for-line port of comp4 hexa). hxc_composite_chain is the closest 'orchestrator' shape but its orchestration target is compression stages, not seed-statistics aggregation; reusing its scaffold provides no LOC savings since none of its primitives are reusable.
wrappers.blocker: no shard contributes statistical aggregation primitives

selftest_mandate_for_wrappers: Each wrapper would need its own selftest (the original blocked components already specify 5/5, 4/4, 3/3 test counts). None of the candidate wrappers reach a state where a meaningful selftest could exist beyond echoing the Python re-implementation back at itself.
conclusion: No wrapping path measurably reduces LOC versus a clean Python rewrite of Comp 1/3/4. The shards' single capability (byte compression) is orthogonal to the missing components' single requirement (numerical projections + statistics).
